subject: Reserved Capacity: term options, ramp start, and invoicing for Velotech
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@velotech.com>
Cc: Sara Lloyd <sara.lloyd@velotech.com>, accounts@velotech.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved Capacity: term options, ramp start, and invoicing for Velotech

Hi Oliver / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion I wanted to put the options on paper so we can align on term length, how you want to phase capacity, and invoicing cadence. High level options we discussed: 

- 12-month reserved commit: higher monthly rate, flexible start window, 1.15x baseline throughput guarantee, lower up-front discount
- 24-month reserved commit: better unit pricing (approx -12%), guaranteed throughput SLAs (p99 latency target), recommended phased ramp over 8 weeks
- 36-month reserved commit: deepest discount (-18%), committed baseline with annual true-up, ability to lock pricing for model upgrades

A few clarifying questions so we can finalize a formal quote and SOW:
1) Desired contract term (12 / 24 / 36 months)?
2) Target capacity at month 3 and month 6 (GPU pool vCPU/GPU count or equivalent TFLOPS), and whether Velotech expects a linear ramp or step increases
3) Preferred invoicing: quarterly arrears, quarterly upfront, or 60% up-front + monthly for the remainder?
4) Any procurement constraints (PO timing, SOC2 evidence window) that should affect the start date?

Proposed start window: earliest 2026-09-01 with a phased activation (week 1: 30% baseline, week 4: 60%, week 8: 100%). We can move the start date later if you need procurement time — that will adjust the discount and invoice timing.

I attached a draft SOW and a pricing table (v3) with line items for burst-capacity and optional audit package. If you can reply with term preference and the month-3/month-6 capacity targets I’ll get a redlined quote back to you within 24 hours.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: 20260803_Velotech_SOW.pdf (SOW, 4 pages), Velotech_pricing_table_v3.xlsx (pricing matrix)
From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@velotech.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved Capacity: term options, ramp start, and invoicing for Velotech

Thanks Rachel — good summary. We prefer keeping the contract as short as possible for now (12 months) because we have uncertain model needs next year. A few notes from our side: 

- Target capacity: month 3 = 40 A100-equivalent GPUs, month 6 = 80 A100-equiv (these include the production and staging pools)
- Ramp: prefer a stepped ramp (month 1: 20 GPUs, month 3: 40, month 6: 80) rather than an 8-week linear ramp — gives us time to validate latency on our side
- Invoicing: procurement wants either quarterly upfront or 60% up-front + net-30 for the remainder; they are unlikely to accept quarterly arrears
- Discount ask: given this is an initial commitment and we may expand, can Redwood do a one-time onboarding credit or a 10% first-year discount on the committed portion? If we go 24 months we could ask for a larger discount, but the business prefers 12 months for flexibility

Please loop in pricing/finance if you need to structure a special invoice. We can also sign the SOW via DocuSign once terms are confirmed.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Reed | VP, Infrastructure
Velotech
oliver.reed@velotech.com

Thanks for the context. Quick thoughts: 

- We can accommodate a 12-month term with a 6-8 week phased validation to reach the committed throughput. For that structure I recommend we keep the onboarding credit limited (max 8%) and tie it to a technical acceptance criteria (TA) at month 3. That protects us if they don't ramp to 40 GPUs by month 3.
- Invoice mechanics: finance prefers quarterly upfront (customer prepays each quarter) for any >$250k quarterly ARR. If Velotech's ARR falls below that threshold we can accept 60% upfront + net-30 for the balance. 
- SLA wording: propose a graduated throughput guarantee: 70% of baseline guaranteed from activation, 90% by month 3 after TA, 100% by month 6. Latency SLOs apply once validation for that pool is complete.
- Pricing: we can offer option B (8% onboarding credit) but we should require DocuSign acceptance of a short technical annex and a PO within 10 business days of signature.

Priyom — can you confirm the billing language and produce redline for option B (12-month + 8% credit + TA)? Also confirm whether we can amortize onboarding credit across invoices or if it needs to be a single invoice credit.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved Capacity: term options, ramp start, and invoicing for Velotech

Agree with Karthik. Finance stance:

- Option A: acceptable only if total contract value (TCV) < $900k. For TCV >= $900k we require quarterly upfront or 60% upfront + remaining on net-30 with credit hold until PO is received.
- Option B (12-mo + 8% credit): fine, but make the credit a one-time invoice credit applied after month 2 following TA confirmation. Do not amortize.
- Option C (24-mo): must include an annual true-up clause and a minimum 9% discount floor (we can give 12% only if they commit to an annual capacity review and 30-day notice for reductions).

I will draft the invoice language and a short billing exhibit for inclusion in the SOW. Rachel — once you confirm which option Velotech wants, I’ll produce the redlined billing exhibit and payment schedule.

-Priyom
Priyom Das | Finance, Redwood Inference

Oliver / Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing your procurement constraints. Based on internal guidance we can present two firm commercial options for signature: 

Option 1 (Velotech preferred): 12-month reserved commit
- Committed baseline: 80 A100-equiv by month 6 (stepped ramp: month 1 = 20, month 3 = 40, month 6 = 80)
- Pricing: standard monthly rate (see attached pricing table)
- Onboarding credit: 8% one-time credit applied as a single invoice credit in month 2 after TA (technical acceptance at month 3 for the 40-GPU milestone)
- Invoicing: 60% up-front at signing, remainder invoiced net-30
- Conditions: PO required within 10 business days of signature; TA milestones documented in the technical annex

Option 2 (price-oriented): 24-month reserved commit
- Committed baseline: 80 A100-equiv with annual true-up
- Pricing: 12% discount on committed baseline
- Invoicing: quarterly upfront
- Conditions: annual review clause for capacity adjustments; 30-day notice for reductions

We attached an updated SOW and the redlined billing exhibit for Option 1 (document names above). If you’re comfortable with Option 1 we can route DocuSign and aim to receive PO + payment to hit an activation start of 2026-09-01. If you prefer Option 2 we’ll share the 24-month contract and updated invoicing schedule.

Please let me know which option you prefer and I’ll trigger the DocuSign flow.

Best,
